newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia bank to open branches in Serb enclave.
newsitem.headline: Croatia bank to open branches in Serb enclave.

text.p: Private Croatia Banka d.d. said on Friday it was ready to open branches in two largest towns of Eastern Slavonia, Croatia's last Serb-held enclave, state news agency HINA reported.
Eastern Slavonia, a fertile and oil-rich plain, is due to revert to Croatian rule by mid-summer and local elections there are tentatively scheduled for mid-March.
Croatia Bank management announced its decision in a letter to Jacques Klein, head of the United Nations Transitional Administration (UNTAES), currently in charge of the enclave.

"In the spirit of the process of peaceful reintegration and pending local elections (in Eastern Slavonia), Croatia Banka will open its branches in Vukovar and Beli Manastir," the bank said in a statement carried by HINA.

The enclave saw some of the bloodiest fighting during Serb minority uprising against Croatia's bid for independence in 1991. Croatia recaptured other Serb-held lands in surprise offensives in 1995. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
